day_shape: 66 items: CENTCOM claims 17 vessels redirected in Arabian Sea blockade while Iran says all Hormuz traffic uses its route, IDF announces killing of Hamas internal-security chief Ladawi, Khamenei issues Hezbollah 'Covenant of Resistance' response, Defa Press quotes Fazaeli saying Iran has no technical barrier to a bomb, EU pledges €3.08m via WFP for refugees in Iran.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz routing standoff
threads.summary: CENTCOM said USS Frank E. Petersen Jr. is enforcing a US blockade that has redirected 17 commercial vessels, disabled 2 and boarded 2, while IRIB cited Marisk data claiming nearly all ships over three days used Iran's designated route. Iranian foreign ministry deputy Gharibabadi said Tehran rejected a US-proposed southern route at Islamabad talks, and IRGC media said the Navy stopped 6 ships attempting an unauthorised transit.

threads.label: Trump-Iran negotiations and threats
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post cited N12 reporting Trump saying the US is negotiating with Iran and will return to war if talks fail, while Times of Israel reported he posted AI-generated images of Iranian ships and energy sites being destroyed. Trump also denied that munitions shortages drove his halt to strikes after 13 days, and Netanyahu is expected to discuss Iran with him in Washington.

threads.label: IDF Gaza strikes and tunnel demolition
threads.summary: The IDF and Shin Bet said they killed Wael Musa Khaled Ladawi, head of Hamas's internal security in central Gaza, in a Deir al-Balah strike on Sunday, and separately killed Islamic Jihad's Amro Abu Alrish, who took part in a hostage release ceremony. The military also said combat engineers demolished a Hamas tunnel stretching hundreds of metres in northern Gaza.

threads.label: Khamenei Hezbollah 'Covenant of Resistance'
threads.summary: Khamenei's office and IRIB pushed a coordinated messaging cycle around the Leader's response to a letter of allegiance from Hezbollah's Secretary-General, declaring defence of Hezbollah Lebanon a strategic policy of the Islamic Republic. A parallel post said there is 'no way forward except struggle and resistance' against the US and Israel.

threads.label: Iran nuclear-weapons capability messaging
threads.summary: Defa Press quoted Fazaeli, of the office preserving Khamenei's works, saying Iran has 'no technical problem' manufacturing atomic weapons and sees no sign of change in the fatwa banning them, requiring only political will. The Jerusalem Post separately ran an opinion piece arguing four months into the Iran campaign the US risks a Vietnam-style gradualism.

threads.label: Yemen–Saudi oil escalation
threads.summary: Defa Press reported Yemen claiming extensive drone attacks on Saudi Arabia's crude oil transmission lines, and the Jerusalem Post reported Iran-backed Houthis escalating threats against Saudi Arabia. The Post cited fears the renewed Yemen activity could disrupt Red Sea shipping.

threads.label: UK–Gulf diplomacy and EU aid to Iran
threads.summary: Downing Street said the Prime Minister spoke to UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan on 26 July, and the Jerusalem Post reported the UK's Islamic Center of England has been granted skilled-worker and religious visa sponsorship rights despite allegations of Iran regime links. UN OCHA/WFP announced a €3.08 million EU contribution to sustain assistance for refugees and conflict-affected people in Iran over 12 months.

events.title: Updating Website and Contact Information, and Authorizations for Payments for Legal Services
events.summary: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) is adopting a final rule to update website and contact information in certain parts of the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR). Additionally, OFAC is amending one CFR Part to update general licenses authorizing payments for legal services from funds originating outside the United States to replace the reporting requirement in the general license with a recordkeeping requirement and correcting typographical errors in two CFR Parts. OFAC is also updating its regulations to correct an erroneous cross-reference.
